# AGENTS.md

Working instructions for this repository — Benson Fung's personal site.

## Overview

- Static site built with Eleventy 3 (ESM config in `eleventy.config.js`).
- `src/` is the source; `docs/` is the local build output. GitHub Pages serves the `gh-pages` branch, published by the deploy workflow (see Publishing).
- One shared layout: `src/_includes/base.njk`. Global site data (name, canonical URL): `src/_data/site.json`.
- Root passthrough files: `robots.txt`, `.nojekyll` (Pages serves the site as plain static files, not Jekyll).

## Development & operations

- Install: `npm install`
- Local preview: `npm run dev` (Eleventy dev server with hot reload)
- Build: `npm run build` — writes to `docs/` (local build output, never committed)
- **Never hand-edit files in `docs/`.** Change `src/` and rebuild.
- After editing, run `npm run build` and sanity-check the generated `docs/*.html` before pushing.
- Push to `master`; the `deploy.yml` workflow builds the site in Actions, uploads the RUM source map, and publishes the output to the `gh-pages` branch. Pages serves `gh-pages` (root). See Publishing below.

## Publishing — GitHub Actions + gh-pages

- `master` holds source only. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs on every push to `master` (plus manual dispatch): checkout with full history → Node 24 → `npm ci` → `npm run build` → verify the build output → deploy the built site to the `gh-pages` branch → upload the RUM source map to Datadog. Pull requests only run the build.
- Pages serves the `gh-pages` branch (root). Switch it in Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source: "Deploy from a branch", branch `gh-pages`, folder `/ (root)`.
- The deploy step works in a throwaway clone and pushes the contents of `docs/` (including `.nojekyll`) to `gh-pages`, one commit per deploy, message `Deploy bfung.github.io from <sha>`. The `master` checkout is never disturbed. Deploys are serialized (`concurrency: pages-deploy`).
- The source-map upload runs after deploy in the same job, using the `DD_API_KEY` repository secret; see Source Code Integration below. The site deploys even if the upload fails.
- `docs/` is a local build artifact: gitignored, never committed, never hand-edited. Local `npm run build` / `npm run dev` still write it for preview.
- Cutover complete (2026-10-25): Pages source switched to `gh-pages` / root, live site verified in the browser, and the committed `docs/` removed from `master` — `master` now holds source only.

## Analytics — Datadog RUM (the site's only analytics)

- Config lives in exactly one place: `src/assets/js/rum-init.src.js` (`service: bfung.github.io`, `env` always `prod`, Datadog site `us3`, `version` = `package.json` version). Change config there; do not duplicate the application ID / client token elsewhere in the repo — they are public browser identifiers and that file is the source of truth.
- **Remote Configuration:** the init also carries a `remoteConfiguration` id (in `rum-init.src.js`) linking the SDK to the remote config managed in Datadog. Until values are configured and published there, the SDK keeps using the init-code values — nothing changes. Once published, remote values override the init values, so check Datadog before assuming the init values are live.
- **Edit the `.src.js`, never the bundle.** `src/assets/js/rum-init.js` is generated by `npm run bundle:rum` (esbuild bundles `@datadog/browser-rum` into a minified IIFE). `npm run build` and `npm run dev` both run `bundle:rum` first. If the bundle is missing or stale in `docs/`, rerun the build; never hand-edit it.
- **Wiring:** `src/_includes/base.njk` loads the bundle in `<head>` with `defer` and the `cacheBust` filter — that covers all 9 main pages. The 16 standalone vibe-redesign templates each load it with a hardcoded `?v=<version>` query instead. **When `package.json` version changes, update that query in all 16 vibe files** (base.njk needs no manual bump) and keep the RUM `version` in step too.
- **Tracking:** multi-page static site, no client router, so default RUM view tracking gives one view per page load and `trackUserInteractions` covers link clicks. No custom views or actions. Heatmaps are on via the same two settings (Session Replay sampled at 20% + `trackUserInteractions`); view them in Datadog under Digital Experience > Product Analytics > Heatmaps — they need replay data, so they populate as sampled sessions with clicks accumulate. Known gaps — do not silently fix, use `data-dd-action-name` only if naming matters later: FamilyTreeMe SVG-node clicks, the project-sort `<select>` change event (not a click), and generic names on button clicks (theme/nav toggles, filter chips).
- **Privacy:** no PII on the site (no email, phone, or zip; FamilyTreeMe uses kinship titles only), no CSP, no other analytics. Session replay samples only public content. RUM beacons to Datadog `us3` are the deliberate exception to the site's otherwise no-third-party-loads rule (previously only Google Fonts + jsDelivr).
- **Source Code Integration (RUM error stack traces):** the RUM bundle's source map is uploaded to Datadog so Error Tracking unminifies stack traces and links frames to the `bfung/bfung.github.com` repo.
  - Method is service + version (not Debug ID): `--service` must equal the RUM `service` (`bfung.github.io`), `--release-version` must equal the RUM `version` (package.json version), `--minified-path-prefix` is `https://bfung.github.io/assets/js` (where the bundle is served). `env` is not part of source-map matching.
  - Maps are generated by `bundle:rum` (`--sourcemap --sources-content=true`); `rum-init.js.map` is gitignored and never published (Eleventy copies only `*.js` from `src/assets/js/`). Only the RUM bundle is minified — `main.js`, `familytreeme.js`, and `guides-diagram.js` are served unminified and need no maps.
  - Upload with `DD_API_KEY=<dedicated key> npm run upload:sourcemaps` (`scripts/upload-sourcemaps.mjs`, `@datadog/datadog-ci`). Order matters: build → commit → push → upload — the script refuses on a dirty tree so the Git metadata datadog-ci collects matches the deployed commit. `npm run upload:sourcemaps -- --dry-run` validates without uploading. Never commit the API key. The deploy workflow runs this automatically on every push to `master`; the local command is for ad-hoc uploads.
  - Datadog-side manual step: install the GitHub integration in Datadog and give it access to `bfung/bfung.github.com`. Verify uploads on the Explore RUM Debug Symbols page.
  - Note: the served bundle ends with a `//# sourceMappingURL=rum-init.js.map` comment; with devtools open the browser 404s fetching the unpublished map — benign, devtools-only.
- **Quick check after a build:** `docs/assets/js/rum-init.js` exists and every built HTML page references it; in Datadog, events should show `service: bfung.github.io`, `env: prod`, and `version` matching `package.json`.

## Site style and design

- CSS architecture: cascade layers — `reset`, `base`, `theme`, `components`, `utilities` — in `src/assets/css/style.css`. Keep new styles in the correct layer; component styles belong in `components`.
- Theming: color comes from CSS custom properties in the `theme` layer. Light and dark modes switch via the `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`; `src/assets/js/main.js` defaults to the OS `prefers-color-scheme` and persists an explicit user choice in localStorage. New UI must work in both themes.
- Color: OKLCH palette — deep indigo accents in light mode, teal-blue accents in dark mode.
- Typography: Outfit for headings, Inter for body, each with system-ui fallbacks. No icon fonts; use inline SVG where icons are needed.
- Layout: fluid, responsive, mobile-first. The resume page has a dedicated print stylesheet — keep print output clean.
- Accessibility: semantic HTML, skip-to-content link, real `alt` text on images, keyboard-reachable controls.
- SEO basics live in the shared layout: canonical URL, Open Graph + Twitter cards, JSON-LD Person schema, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`. Keep metadata current when URLs or page purposes change.

## Vibe carryover

- A VibeRedesign page's own styling cannot follow a visitor onto a differently-marked-up page, so carryover is token-level, not a layout clone: `src/assets/js/vibe.js` remembers the last vibe in localStorage (`bfung-vibe`) and sets `data-vibe` on `<html>`; `src/assets/css/vibes.css` (unlayered, so it beats style.css's layered theme tokens) re-skins shared-layout pages from that vibe's palette and type. All 16 vibe templates load vibe.js; the shared layout loads it synchronously in `<head>` before the stylesheets, so there is no unthemed flash.
- Precedence in vibe.js: `?vibe=<slug>` (or `?vibe=none` to clear) wins; then a `/vibe-redesign/<slug>/` URL records that vibe; then visiting main Home (`/` or `/index.html`) clears the stored vibe and restores the original theme; otherwise the stored vibe is re-applied. The hub (`/vibe-redesign/`) records nothing, so it shows the carried vibe. The banner in base.njk ("Viewing in the X vibe · Exit vibe") is the other way out; while a vibe is active the light/dark toggle has no visible effect.
- Scope limits: only pages rendered by base.njk carry a vibe (Resume, Projects, Guides, FamilyTreeMe, AI Financing Map, hub). Page-specific art (FamilyTreeMe SVG, AI Financing Map D3 colours) keeps its own palette. External project links leave the site, so no vibe can follow them. Keep the slug allowlist in vibe.js and the token blocks in vibes.css in step; palette values are copied from each vibe's own `:root` tokens, with two documented legibility deviations (mid-century accent darkened, neubrutalist accent = ink with yellow as tag/shadow).

## Conventions

- Pages are Nunjucks templates (`.njk`) with front matter (`title`, `description`) consumed by the layout.
- **Content is single-sourced in `src/_data/`**: `profile.json` (title, taglines, summary, location, socials), `resume.json` (experience, education, skills), `projects.json`, `guides.json`. The main Home/Resume AND all eight VibeRedesign designs render from these files — edit the data, never the templates, to change content. Vibe templates loop over the data in their own markup; never use Nunjucks `selectattr` to pick a social (it silently does not filter here) — loop and match on `s.id` instead.
- Assets live under `src/assets/` and are passthrough-copied to `docs/assets/`.
- Reference global data from `src/_data/site.json` rather than hardcoding the site URL in templates.
- Commit and push promptly after a change is verified — uncommitted work in this checkout was once lost mid-session (working tree reverted to HEAD with no trace), so don't leave changes uncommitted across long detours.
- Keep braces balanced in `style.css`: a single stray `}` once caused the CSS parser to silently drop the entire `@layer utilities` block (visible skip link, dead `.sr-only`). After structural CSS edits, verify the parsed stylesheet in the browser (e.g. check `document.styleSheets` layer blocks), not just the source.
